lines.japanese: ようがす。よござんす監督。
lines.english: Very good. Very well indeed, Director.

lines.japanese: そこまでおっしゃるなら行きやしょう。今こそ行きやしょう。
lines.english: If you insist, then go I shall. Now is the hour.

lines.japanese: 「先生、今日のパンツは何色ですか」
lines.english: “Ms. Tama, what color is your underwear today?”

lines.japanese: 無言。
lines.english: Wordlessness.

lines.japanese: 沈黙というより無言です。
lines.english: Not silence so much as the total absence of words.

lines.japanese: いづみさんはあのぴんと背筋を伸ばした姿勢で、前衛芸術の奇妙なオブジェでも鑑賞するみたいに俺の目を直視しています。
lines.english: Izumi held herself ramrod straight and stared directly into my eyes as though contemplating some peculiar object in an avant-garde exhibition.
“Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: やがて彼女は、両手で外した眼鏡をことりとテーブルの上に置き、静かに口を開きました。
lines.english: At length, she removed her glasses with both hands, set them softly on the table, and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「すみません、その前にこちらからお伺いしてもよろしいでしょうか」
lines.english: “Before that, may I ask you a question?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、僕のっすか？　僕のでしたら今日は、牡丹と薔薇のビキニパン──」
lines.english: “Mine? Today I’m wearing bikini briefs with peonies and roses—”

lines.japanese: 「実際の記事の方もこういった方向性になるんですか？」
lines.english: “Will the actual article be taking this sort of approach as well?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、はい、そうですよ。担当編集からはそのように言いつかってます。ま、男性誌ですから」
lines.english: “What? Oh, yes. Those were my editor’s instructions. It is a men’s magazine, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: いづみさんは強張った笑顔で頷いたあと、真下を向いて溜息を落とし、またすぐに向きなおりました。
lines.english: Izumi nodded with a stiff smile, looked down and sighed, then immediately turned back to me.

lines.japanese: 「白です」
lines.english: “White.”
“Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 唐突な回答──しかも声がマジでした。
lines.english: The answer came out of nowhere—and her voice was deadly serious.

lines.japanese: 「あー……はい、白ですか」
lines.english: “Ah... yes. White.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「……だったと思います」
lines.english: “...I think.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は座ったまま、ささっと体を横へ向けました。
lines.english: Still seated, she swiftly turned her body to one side.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待ってください」
lines.english: “One moment, please.”

lines.japanese: 何かと思えば、両手でズボンの履き口を引っぱり、テーブルの下でその中をこっそり覗いています。
lines.english: Wondering what she meant, I watched her pull open the waistband of her trousers with both hands and furtively peer inside beneath the table.

lines.japanese: 「すみません、ベージュでした」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. Beige.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ……」
lines.english: “Goodness...”

lines.japanese: もぎたての個人情報はなんだか生々しくて、聞いたこっちが引いてしまいました。ていうか、あまりに飾らないその色がまた生々しいです。
lines.english: This freshly harvested piece of personal information felt so raw that even I, the man who had asked for it, recoiled. The utter lack of ornament in the color only made it rawer.

lines.japanese: や、たしかに伺いましたけどね？　そんな冷静にお答いただけるとは予想外です。カケルくんの前情報と違って、ぜんぜん場が暖まりません。これでは、まるで俺ひとりが馬鹿みたいです。
lines.english: Yes, I had asked. But I never expected such a level-headed answer. Contrary to Kakeru's intelligence, the room had not warmed up in the slightest. At this rate I looked like the only idiot here.

lines.japanese: 「ていうか俺……ばか？」
lines.english: “Wait... am I an idiot?”

lines.japanese: 「仕事ですから軽蔑はしていません」
lines.english: “Since this is business, I do not despise you.”

lines.japanese: 独り言に返答されてるし……しかも否定はされてないし……。
lines.english: She answered my muttering—and failed to deny it.

lines.japanese: ふたたび管制塔の指示を仰ごうと振りかえれば、俯いて顔を隠したカケルくんは、口元を抑えながらぷるぷると肩を揺らしていました。
lines.english: I turned to request fresh instruction from the control tower. Kakeru had lowered his head to hide his face; one hand covered his mouth while his shoulders shook.

lines.japanese: 「あの、監督ソレさぁ……」
lines.english: “Director... that thing you're doing right now...”

lines.japanese: ええ。
lines.english: Yes.

lines.japanese: ええ、はい。そうですよね、はい。
lines.english: Yes, of course. Naturally.

lines.japanese: いや、俺もね、お下劣トークから始まる人間関係なんてありえないとは思ってたんですけどね。
lines.english: I mean, I’d thought myself that you couldn’t possibly start a relationship with filthy conversation.

lines.japanese: 「先生」
lines.english: “Ms. Tama.”

lines.japanese: 俺はテーブルに両手を付いて身を乗りだしました。
lines.english: I planted both hands on the table and leaned toward her.

lines.japanese: 「変えましょう。やっぱり先生も、男の子向けテイストは抵抗あるでしょう」
lines.english: “Let's change course. You must have reservations about this whole ‘for the boys’ angle too.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、構いません」
lines.english: “No. I don’t mind.”

lines.japanese: いづみさんは自棄になったとしか思えない挑戦的な声で言いました。
lines.english: Izumi answered with a defiance that could only have been born of desperation.

lines.japanese: 「……ほんとにぃ？」
lines.english: “Are you suuuure?”

lines.japanese: 「『男性誌ですから』」
lines.english: “‘It is a men’s magazine, after all.’”

lines.japanese: 「無理してません？」
lines.english: “You aren’t forcing yourself?”

lines.japanese: 「たしかにそういう観点で読まれる方がいたのは予想外でしたけれど、送り手の意図と受け手の印象に齟齬が生じるのは、創作の楽しみのひとつでもあります」
lines.english: “I admit I had not expected anyone to read it from that perspective. But the discrepancy between the creator's intention and the audience's impression is one of the pleasures of making art.”

lines.japanese: や、楽しみとか言いつつ、声のトーンがぜんぜん楽しそうじゃないんですけど。
lines.english: She called it a pleasure, but her voice contained none whatsoever.

lines.japanese: ていうか、あの桃色エッセイのまだ見ぬ６ページ目以降にはそんな、多面的なブンガク性が潜んでいるわけですか？
lines.english: More to the point, did that racy memoir really have such many-faceted Literary Depths lurking in the pages I hadn’t read, from page six onward?

lines.japanese: 「えと……先生はどういった狙いというか、テーマのもとにあの作品を書かれたわけですか」
lines.english: “Then... what intention or theme led you to write the work?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん、老境に至った人間が想う、ひとや世のはかなさです」
lines.english: “Naturally, the transience of people and the world as contemplated by a human being in the twilight of life.”

lines.japanese: 「高齢化社会への提言！？」
lines.english: “A policy proposal for an aging society?!”

lines.japanese: え、ネイキッド・アクトレスの赤裸々ラじゃなくて？　ていうか老境に至った人間って誰？
lines.english: Wait—what had happened to the naked actress and her bare-all nakeditude? And who exactly had entered the twilight of life?

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのう、先生……あの作品ってたしか、先生の実体験ですよね？」
lines.english: “Um, Ms. Tama... that work was based on your own experiences, wasn't it?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか。そんなわけないじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Of course not. How could it be?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「違うんですか！？」
lines.english: “It wasn’t?!”

lines.japanese: いったん生返事をしておいてから一拍置いて訊きなおすという、いづみさんの癖がうつってしまうほどに俺は動揺していました。
lines.english: My shock was so complete that I had caught Izumi's habit: give a vague answer, wait one beat, and only then ask the real question.

lines.japanese: 「違います。面白い冗談ですね。あーははは」
lines.english: “No. What an amusing joke. Ha. Ha. Ha.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はははー……」
lines.english: “Ha... ha ha...”

lines.japanese: え、ちょっと待って……てことは？
lines.english: Wait. Then what did this mean?

lines.japanese: 俺がカケルくんに謀られたのは下ネタ云々だけじゃなくて、もっと根本的なところで……？
lines.english: Had Kakeru deceived me about more than the dirty jokes—something much more fundamental...?

lines.japanese: つまり……？
lines.english: Which meant...?

lines.japanese: このひと、あの本の作者じゃない！？
lines.english: This woman hadn't written that book at all?!

lines.japanese: 「お、おおっと！　いかん、もうこんな時間だ！」
lines.english: “Oh! Goodness! Look at the time!”

lines.japanese: 俺は早急にカケルくんを問いただす必要があると感じ、この場を撤収することにしました。
lines.english: Feeling an urgent need to interrogate Kakeru, I elected to withdraw from the field at once.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、それじゃ今日は本当にもう。ええ、貴重なお話をありがとうございました。ええ、ええ」
lines.english: “Well, I really must be going. Thank you very much for the invaluable conversation. Yes. Yes indeed.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……いえ、こちらこそお世話になります」
lines.english: “Oh... no, thank you. I appreciate your help.”

lines.japanese: 目を合わさずにぺこぺこお辞儀しながら席を立つと、対面の女性もゆっくり腰を上げてきっちり頭を下げてくれました。
lines.english: I rose without meeting her eyes, bobbing my head repeatedly. The woman opposite me slowly stood as well and gave me a proper bow.

lines.japanese: いたたまれなくなって走りだした俺。
lines.english: Unable to endure another moment, I ran.

lines.japanese: あっ。
lines.english: Ah.

lines.japanese: しまった。思わず飛びだしたはいいが、中にカケル君を置きっぱなしだった。
lines.english: Damn. I had bolted outside and left Kakeru behind.

lines.japanese: 仕方ない、出てくるまでちょっと待つか……。
lines.english: Nothing for it. I would wait until he came out...

lines.japanese: いやしかし、こうなったのは彼のせい。呑気に出迎えてやる義理もありません。ていうか、あんまりここに長居してたら、あの多摩いづみ的なひとから逃げてきた意味が──
lines.english: No. This was his fault. I owed him no leisurely welcome. Besides, if I lingered here much longer, fleeing that person who was supposed to be Tama Izumi would have accomplished nothing—

lines.japanese: 「あの」
lines.english: “Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、ごめんなさい！」
lines.english: “Aah! I’m sorry!”

lines.japanese: 「その、本当に……どのように書いていただいても構いませんから」
lines.english: “Truly... you may write it however you see fit.”
“Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、雑誌のカラーや読者層に合わせて書いていただければ」
lines.english: “Please shape it to suit the magazine's character and readership.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……はは、まあ……」
lines.english: “Oh... ha ha. Of course...”

lines.japanese: 曖昧に笑いながらお茶を濁す俺。
lines.english: I gave an uncertain laugh and tried to muddle through.

lines.japanese: てか、わざわざそんなことを言うために追っかけてきたんですか、このひとは。
lines.english: Had this woman actually chased me down merely to say that?

lines.japanese: 「よろしくお願いします。どんな形であれ取りあげていただけるのは……」
lines.english: “Please. Whatever form it takes, simply having the work covered...”

lines.japanese: 彼女は頭を下げてから、ひどく頼りない声で言いました。
lines.english: She bowed, then continued in a terribly fragile voice.

lines.japanese: 「ひとりでも多くのひとに書いたものを読んでもらえるっていうのは、やっぱり、嬉しいんです」
lines.english: “Knowing that even one more person may read something I wrote... really does make me happy.”

lines.japanese: そして、目の前のうさんくさい青二才を信じきって言いました。
lines.english: And placing absolute faith in the dubious young greenhorn before her, she said—

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんの記事、楽しみにしてます」
lines.english: “I’m looking forward to your article, Mr. Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「や、あの、ええと」
lines.english: “Well, I... um...”

lines.japanese: その、おそらく多摩いづみさんではない誰かの、母親を見つけた迷子みたいな笑顔を向けられて──
lines.english: Someone who probably wasn’t Tama Izumi smiled at me like a lost child who had found her mother—

lines.japanese: 「えと……その……ご」
lines.english: “Um... well... you—”

lines.japanese: ──鷲介くんの逆博愛精神は、無意識のうちに俺の首を縦に振らせていました。
lines.english: —and young Shusuke’s belief in universal love—with everyone loving me—made me nod before I knew what I was doing.

lines.japanese: 「ご期待ください」
lines.english: “You won’t be disappointed.”

lines.japanese: もしかして俺は、無責任な約束をしてしまったのでしょうか。
lines.english: Had I just made a promise I had no right to make?
